messages.subject: negative estimation of STD_genotype
parts:
Hi,
I am running a analysis and I am getting negative estimation of STD_genotype (negative additive genetic variance);  I don't know if negative STD_genotype  make sense in the research. How can I explain this situation? It's whether that means there's something wrong with the model I built
 here you have an example: 
F1=~A19  -0.07 (Unstand_Est) 0.19 (Unstand_SE)  -0.64 (STD_Genotype) 1.64 (STD_Genotype_SE)
Thank you for your help!

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: negative estimation of STD_genotype
parts:
Hello, 

If you are taking about a negative residual variance then you can see the posting here for an explanation and solution: 
https://groups.google.com/g/genomic-sem-users/c/A9IAnJugoKM/m/eaxILVNPCAAJ

It looks like from the output you posted that you are getting a negative factor loading. This can happen if the variable has a negative genetic correlation with the majority of the other traits that load onto that same factor. In this instance, this would not be considered something that needs to be fixed, but rather is an approximate recapitulation of the observed data in the factor model results. 

Best, 
  Andrew
